verdict.rationale: Cloudflare documents its own event-triggered automation. Event subscriptions publish account events (e.g. a Worker build completing, an R2 bucket being created) to a queue automatically, and Workers consume them to run custom logic; Workflows can also pause for external events. The 'rules' are code you write in a consumer Worker, not a declarative rule definition, and cron is a recurring schedule rather than an event trigger. missing for 10: declarative rule/condition definitions without writing code, documented filtering or matching of events to actions, independent hands-on corroboration of event-triggered automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: When you subscribe to these events, your queue will automatically start receiving messages when the events occur.

Cloudflare products (e.g., KV, Workers AI, Workers) can publish structured events to a queue, which you can then consume with Workers or HTTP pull consumers to build custom workflows, integrations, or logic.
The ability to pause for external events or approvals
